description: Publish operations to a persisted query list, the same write that `rover persisted-queries publish` performs. A persisted query list is the set of operations a router accepts when it is configured to reject anything else. Operations you do not mention stay in the list unchanged: pass operations to add or replace entries, and remove to drop them. Returns the new revision and the total operation count, or reports that nothing changed. Use GetPersistedQueryListStatus to find the list ID and its current revision. Provide the graph ID and the persisted query list ID.

GraphQLDocument.description: A GraphQL document, such as a schema in SDL syntax.

PersistedQueryIdInput.description: Full identifier for an operation in a Persisted Query List.

clientName.description: An optional client name to associate with the operation. Two operations with the same ID but different client names are treated as distinct operations. An operation with the same ID and a null client name is treated as a distinct operation as well.

id.description: An opaque identifier for this operation. For a given client name, this should map uniquely to an operation body; editing the body should generally result in a new ID. Apollo's tools generally use the lowercase hex SHA256 of the operation body.

PersistedQueryInput.description: Operations to be published to the Persisted Query List.

body.description: The GraphQL document for this operation, including all necessary fragment definitions.

clientName.description: An optional client name to associate with the operation. Two operations with the same ID but different client names are treated as distinct operations.

id.description: An opaque identifier for this operation. This should map uniquely to an operation body; editing the body should generally result in a new ID. Apollo's tools generally use the lowercase hex SHA256 of the operation body.

name.description: A name for the operation. Typically this is the name of the actual GraphQL operation in the body. This does not need to be unique within a Persisted Query List; as a client project evolves and its operations change, multiple operations with the same name (but different body and id) can be published.

name: PublishPersistedQueries
